findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve every unresolved `release-version-` alert whose exact reason (not just name) is no longer in the current withheld set, and add a unit test for the archived→missing flip.

findings.finding: Alert resolution is keyed on name while creation/dedup is keyed on reason. When a withheld name changes reason (e.g. archived version is later deleted, archived→missing, or un-archived then deleted), plan_release_alerts creates a new `release-version-missing:<name>` alert. It does not resolve the existing `release-version-archived:<name>` alert, because that name is still withheld. Two unresolved alerts then name the same release.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (plan_release_alerts) vs AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Version 2.4 archived → alert archived:2.4; operator deletes it → missing:2.4 added while archived:2.4 stays open
findings.suggested_fix: In plan_release_alerts compute current_reasons = {f"release-version-{w['reason']}:{w['release']}"}. Create an alert for each reason not unresolved, and resolve each unresolved `release-version-*` alert whose reason is not in current_reasons. Add test: unresolved archived:2.4 + withheld missing:2.4 → one new missing alert + one resolution of the archived uuid.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make alert resolution key on the full (name, reason) pair so a reason change resolves the old alert, and add a plan_release_alerts test for an archived→missing transition.
evidence: "a new alert ... per withheld name without an unresolved alert of that reason"
"{"resolved": true, ...} per unresolved `release-version-` alert whose name is no longer withheld"
findings.finding: Alert creation is keyed on the full reason, but resolution is keyed only on the release name. When a withheld name changes reason (an archived version is later deleted, or a missing version is created archived), a new alert with the new reason is written. The old alert is never resolved because its name is still withheld. The ticket ends up with two unresolved alerts for one release.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (plan_release_alerts); AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Pass 1: 2.4 is archived, so release-version-archived:2.4 is raised. A user then deletes the version. Pass 2 raises release-version-missing:2.4 and leaves the archived alert open, giving two unresolved alerts for 2.4.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each unresolved release-version- alert whose exact reason is not in the current withheld set {release-version-<reason>:<name>}. Add a unit test: an unresolved archived:2.4 alert plus withheld missing:2.4 yields one resolution and one new alert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In plan_release_alerts, resolve every unresolved `release-version-*` alert whose (reason, name) pair is no longer the current withheld pair, so a missing↔archived change resolves the old alert and raises the new one; add a unit test for that transition.

findings.finding: Alert creation is keyed by reason (`release-version-<missing|archived>:<name>`), but resolution only fires for a name that is 'no longer withheld'. If a withheld version changes from missing to archived (or back), the old-reason alert is never resolved, because the name is still withheld, and a second alert with the new reason is added. The ticket ends up with two unresolved alerts for one release.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (plan_release_alerts); AC 'exactly one unresolved BRIDGE_ALERT naming it'
scenarios: Pass 1: 2.4 is missing, so the missing alert is raised. Someone creates 2.4 and archives it. Pass N: 2.4 is withheld as archived, so the archived alert is raised and the missing alert stays unresolved, leaving two unresolved alerts naming 2.4.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the resolution rule to: for each unresolved `release-version-` alert, resolve it unless its full reason equals the current `release-version-<reason>:<name>` of a withheld record. Add a unit test: an unresolved missing:2.4 alert plus 2.4 withheld as archived gives one resolution and one new archived alert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the 'fakes record every call' premise with a check that can actually see a version create: a static scan of the src/rebar/reconciler adapter modules for the version-create endpoint/method, plus a fake that fails on any unknown attribute.

tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py:33 `self.write_calls: list[str] = []  # every non-read client call`; read methods (search_issues, get_comments, get_issue_by_rest, get_issue_property) record nothing
tests/integration/reconciler/test_reconcile_releases_roundtrip.py:64-71 patches `_load_acli` and `_load_reconcile_backend` to the shared fake, so the real adapters are not exercised
findings.finding: The no-create acceptance criterion relies on a false claim: 'the stateful fakes record every call'. The shared `_FakeJiraState.write_calls` only records non-read calls the fake defines. The fake replaces the real Cloud and DC adapters, so a version create inside acli_rest.py or _issues.py never reaches it, and a call to a create method the fake doesn't define raises AttributeError instead of being recorded. Asserting that no recorded call is a create cannot show that no bridge code path creates a Jira version.
findings.location: Approach §6 'Never create versions'; AC 'No bridge code path creates a Jira version; pinned by the fake-transport assertion'
scenarios: A later change adds a `create_version` call to acli_rest.py using `_direct_rest_post_raw('/rest/api/3/version', ...)`; the integration fake never sees it and the test stays green.
Differ code calls `client.create_version(...)`; the fake raises AttributeError, a broad `except` may swallow it, and nothing is recorded, so 'no create recorded' still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a structural test that greps or AST-scans every module under src/rebar/reconciler (including adapters/jira and adapters/jira_datacenter) for `/rest/api/[23]/version` POSTs and for `create_version` / `client.create_version` calls, and asserts there are none. In the integration fake, add a `__getattr__` that records and fails on any unknown member, so a create-shaped call can't vanish into an AttributeError.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record a sink entry only when fixVersions was observed (a list) AND availability is known, and add a test that an unobserved fixVersions snapshot neither raises nor resolves any alert.
evidence: outbound_releases.py:30-32: `if not isinstance(fix_versions, list): return []` — 'a snapshot that never fetched the field cannot be read as "Jira has no versions"'
Plan: "`release_mutations_for` records `sink[local_id] = (jira_key, withheld)` for every bound ticket diffed with known availability"
findings.finding: _diff_releases returns [] early when the snapshot's `fixVersions` is absent or not a list (unobserved). The plan has release_mutations_for record `sink[local_id] = (jira_key, withheld)` for every ticket diffed with known availability. An unobserved snapshot would therefore record an empty withheld list, and write_release_alerts would resolve every open release alert on that ticket. The next observed pass would raise them again, so alerts churn.
findings.location: Approach step 3 (release_mutations_for sink) / step 5
scenarios: A bound ticket's snapshot or direct GET has no fixVersions key, so its open release-version-missing alert is resolved even though the release is still withheld; the next pass raises it again.
findings.suggested_fix: Have _diff_releases signal 'unobserved' (e.g. return None for withheld) and skip the sink write in release_mutations_for in that case, the same way an unknown availability map is handled.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short 'Failure-disposition contract' stating, per arm (version-read error, alert-write error, add under unknown availability), whether it is transient/retried-next-pass or fatal, and what the operator sees.
evidence: "a read error leaves that project absent = unknown"
"`outbound_pass` calls it after the diff, only when `ctx.persist`"
No statement of what a raising _write_event_file or the DC `_call_logged`/`_unwrap` error does to the pass
findings.finding:
The plan adds new failure arms but states no explicit disposition for each.
(a) A version-read error per project: is it transient and retried next pass, logged or warned, and does it abort only that project?
(b) A failed alert write in _write_event_file: does it abort the whole outbound pass (fatal), or is it logged while other tickets continue?
(c) Under unknown availability, the add still 400s and is only logged. The plan should confirm this degraded leg is accepted as non-fatal and retried each pass, rather than masking the read failure.
findings.location: Approach steps 2 and 5; Testing 'a failing version read writes no alert and resolves none'
scenarios: The DC project_versions call raises an auth error every pass. The behavior silently reverts to logged 400s with no surfaced signal.
The tracker dir is unwritable mid-pass. It is unspecified whether the pass fails or the alerts are dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: For example: a version-read error is transient. It is logged at WARNING, that project is treated as unknown (prior behavior), and it is retried next pass. An alert-write error is logged and that ticket's alerts are skipped, with no pass abort. An add 400 under unknown availability remains logged only and is retried next pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make write_release_alerts best-effort per alert (catch and log each write failure, continue, never fail the pass); because dedupe is state-based, a dropped write is retried on the next pass. Add a test where the writer raises.
evidence: inbound_translate.py:175-179: `write_lock(..., attempts=1)` → `raise TimeoutError`
run_differs.py:43,64: `except Exception: # observability only; never break the pass`
Plan: "writes each as a `BRIDGE_ALERT` via `inbound_translate._write_event_file`; `outbound_pass` calls it after the diff"
findings.finding: write_release_alerts calls inbound_translate._write_event_file during the outbound phase, and the plan specifies no failure isolation. _write_event_file raises TimeoutError on a single-attempt lock timeout and can be refused by seam screening. Every existing outbound-phase alert emitter (_emit_outbound_field_alerts, _emit_recovery_failure_alerts, _emit_create_identity_alert) is best-effort and never fails the pass. One failed write here could abort the whole reconcile pass, including unrelated ticket sync.
findings.location: Approach step 5 (write_release_alerts) / outbound_pass call site
scenarios: Contention on the lock during a pass makes the first alert write raise TimeoutError, so the outbound phase errors out and no mutations are dispatched.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each _write_event_file call in try/except Exception with a stderr warning, matching the run_differs alert emitters. Note that the next pass retries naturally because dedupe reads ticket state.

evidence: "reads it once per pass for projects ... of bound tickets that have releases or an unresolved `release-version-` alert"

The plan does not say what happens if the ticket is unbound, closed, or excluded from the outbound diff after an alert is raised. Such an alert would stay open indefinitely.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether alert resolution is gated on a successful Jira add of that release, and state the alert disposition when the add fails after the version becomes available; add an integration case for it.
evidence: "`outbound_pass` calls it after the diff, only when `ctx.persist`"
"per unresolved `release-version-` alert whose name is no longer withheld"
findings.finding: Alert resolution is planned from the diff, and the write happens 'after the diff', independent of whether the now-dispatchable Jira add actually succeeds. If the pass-3 add fails (a transient error, or a 400 for another reason), the alert is already resolved. The release is still absent from Jira and the only signal reverts to a log line.
findings.location: Approach step 5 ('outbound_pass calls it after the diff'); AC 'Once the version exists, the next pass writes it and resolves the alert'

findings.suggested_fix: Write resolutions only after the dispatch for that ticket reports success for the release. On failure, leave the alert unresolved; it is retried on the next pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what happens to unresolved release-version- alerts on tickets that are no longer bound or diffed (resolve on unbind, or explicitly accept them as permanent and document it).
evidence: "for projects (the bound key's prefix) of bound tickets that have releases or an unresolved `release-version-` alert"
"`release_mutations_for` records `sink[local_id] = ...` for every bound ticket diffed with known availability"
findings.finding: The alert lifecycle has no retirement path for tickets that stop being diffed. Resolutions are only planned for tickets placed in the sink ('every bound ticket diffed with known availability'). A ticket that is unbound, whose binding moves projects, or that the outbound pass otherwise skips keeps its unresolved release-version- alerts forever.
findings.location: Approach steps 2–3 (selection of projects / sink population)
scenarios: A ticket with an open release-version-missing:2.4 alert is unbound from Jira. It is never diffed again, so the alert never resolves.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach §5, drop the unconsumed `release` key from the alert payload (or name its reader). State that `plan_release_alerts` gets the name from compiled-state `reason` by stripping the `release-version-<kind>:` prefix, since `process_bridge_alert` keeps only uuid/reason/timestamp/resolved.
evidence: Plan: a new alert `{"reason": "release-version-<missing|archived>:<name>", "tag": "release-version-<missing|archived>", "release": name}`
Plan: resolution 'per unresolved `release-version-` alert whose name is no longer withheld' — the name has to come from compiled state
src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:266-273 — process_bridge_alert appends only {uuid, reason, timestamp, resolved}; `release`/`tag` are not kept in state
Only existing BRIDGE_ALERT precedent (dispatch_one.py:253-259) has `reason` + `tag` and no name-duplicating key
findings.finding: The new alert payload stores the release name twice: in `reason` (`release-version-<kind>:<name>`) and in a separate `release` key. Nothing in the plan reads `release`. The existing reducer keeps only `uuid`/`reason`/`timestamp`/`resolved` for each alert in `state.bridge_alerts`. So `plan_release_alerts(ticket, withheld)`, which reads unresolved alerts from compiled ticket state, cannot see `release` and has to parse the name out of `reason` anyway. The extra key has no consumer and invites a lookup that silently returns nothing.
findings.location: Approach §5 (Alerts) — `plan_release_alerts` alert shape `{"reason": ..., "tag": ..., "release": name}`
scenarios: The implementer writes the resolution branch as `alert.get("release")` over `ticket["bridge_alerts"]`. That is always None, so alerts are never resolved, or are resolved on every pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Use alert shape `{"reason": "release-version-<kind>:<name>", "tag": "release-version-<kind>"}` and say that the name used for matching and resolution is `reason.split(":", 1)[1]` from `ticket["bridge_alerts"]` entries whose reason starts with `release-version-`.

The plan does not state what prevents two overlapping reconcile passes (or a retried pass after a partial write) from both seeing 'no unresolved alert' and writing duplicates. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Seed the transport tests with fixtures copied from real Cloud and DC version responses (including the Version-resource shape after `_unwrap`) and document why they are faithful, or name a live smoke check.

AC runs `env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify` — no live exercise
findings.finding: The new version-read transports are validated only against self-authored fakes. These are a mock DC client returning whatever `project_versions` yields, and a stubbed `_direct_rest_get`. The plan gives no rationale that the fake response shape matches production. For example, python-jira's `project_versions` returns Version resource objects rather than dicts, and the Cloud JSON carries `archived` as a boolean. The `{"name","archived"}` mapping could pass offline and break live, and the release flow would then silently degrade.
findings.location: Testing 'Transports: Cloud reads GET /rest/api/3/project/REB/versions; DC calls project_versions("REB"); both map to {"name","archived"}'
scenarios: The real DC client returns Version objects, and the mapping indexes v["name"], raising TypeError. With read error = unknown, the read always fails, and withholding and alerts never activate in production.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that `plan_release_alerts` gets each existing alert's name and kind by parsing `reason` (`release-version-<kind>:<name>`), because the reducer does not keep the `release`/`tag` keys, and add a test that drives it from reducer-folded ticket state.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:266-272: an unresolved alert is stored as `{"uuid", "reason", "timestamp", "resolved": False}`; `data['release']` and `data['tag']` are not copied
Plan alert shape: `{"reason": "release-version-<missing|archived>:<name>", "tag": ..., "release": name}`
findings.finding: The plan says 'The reducer already folds both shapes', but `process_bridge_alert` keeps only `uuid`, `reason`, `timestamp` and `resolved` on each `state['bridge_alerts']` entry. The `release` and `tag` keys the plan writes are dropped. `plan_release_alerts(ticket, withheld)` must find 'unresolved `release-version-` alerts whose name is no longer withheld' from reduced ticket state, so it has to parse the name out of `reason`. If it reads `alert['release']`, it gets None, every alert looks stale, and each pass resolves and then re-raises it.
findings.location: Approach §5 'Alerts' — `plan_release_alerts` and 'The reducer already folds both shapes (`reducer/_processors.process_bridge_alert`)'
scenarios: Pass 2: the ticket's folded alert has no `release` key; a lookup keyed on `release` decides the name is no longer withheld, writes a resolution, then writes a new alert in the same pass, breaking 'pass 2 writes nothing'.
findings.suggested_fix: In §5, specify that unresolved release alerts are found by `reason.startswith('release-version-')`, with the name taken as `reason.split(':', 1)[1]` and the kind as the prefix before the colon. Add a unit test that feeds `plan_release_alerts` a ticket whose `bridge_alerts` came from `process_bridge_alert`, not hand-built dicts carrying `release`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the DC `get_project_versions` unwraps each item (`[_unwrap(v) for v in versions]`) before mapping to `{name, archived}`, and have the DC unit test's fake return objects that carry `.raw`.
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:22-30: `raw = getattr(obj, 'raw', None); return raw if raw is not None else obj`
Compare _base.py:106 `batch = [_unwrap(issue) for issue in results]`: list results are unwrapped one item at a time elsewhere
findings.finding: The DC read is planned as `self._client.project_versions(key)` 'through `_call_logged`/`_unwrap`', but `_unwrap` only strips `.raw` from a single object. A list has no `.raw` and comes back unchanged, so the library's version objects would reach the mapping step still wrapped. The planned DC unit test ('DC calls `project_versions("REB")`; maps to {name, archived}') would pass against a fake that returns plain dicts while the real path gets wrapped objects.

findings.finding: The plan says the alert data includes `tag` and `release`. But process_bridge_alert folds only `uuid`, `reason`, `timestamp` and `resolved` into `state.bridge_alerts`, so `release` and `tag` do not exist on the ticket state that plan_release_alerts reads. Dedupe and resolution must recover the name by parsing `reason` (the text after the `release-version-<kind>:` prefix). The plan doesn't say this, and an implementer who looks for `alert["release"]` will see no match. That would raise a duplicate alert every pass and never resolve any.

findings.finding: The DC read depends on `self._client.project_versions(key)` from pycontribs `jira`, and on each returned Version's `.raw` carrying `name` and `archived`. Nothing in the repo or the installed environment confirms this: `jira.JIRA.project_versions` resolved UNRESOLVED (package not installed) and no test references it. The plan's DC test ('DC calls `project_versions("REB")`') runs against an injected fake. A fake accepts whatever method name and payload shape the plan defines, so a wrong method name or a raw shape without `archived` would pass every test. In production it would then either raise on every pass, which the plan's error handling turns into permanent 'unknown' with silent fallback to the old 400-on-add behavior, or treat every version as available.

findings.finding: The Cloud endpoint `GET /rest/api/3/project/{key}/versions` is new: no existing code calls it, so it is a new endpoint surface on a vendor the code already uses. The plan says it is 'documented unpaginated' and that each element yields `{"name","archived"}`, but gives no doc reference or recorded response. It also does not say what read permission is needed (Browse Projects on that project), or what happens when a project key is unknown or not visible to the bridge user (404). The Cloud transport test only checks that the request path is built correctly. If the response shape is wrong, for example the payload is wrapped or `archived` is missing, no test catches it.

scenarios: A non-list body, or elements missing `archived`, get mapped as available: archived versions are sent as adds and fail with 400 as before, with no alert.
The bridge user lacks Browse Projects on a sibling project: a 404 or 403 is treated as unknown, so that project's releases go unchecked and the plan says nothing about it.
findings.suggested_fix: In `get_project_versions`: `data = self._direct_rest_get(...)`; if `not isinstance(data, list)`, raise ValueError so `read_release_availability` treats the project as unknown. Map each dict element to `{"name": v["name"], "archived": bool(v.get("archived", False))}`. Add a test fixture copied from the documented sample response, and in docs/jira-sync-setup.md note that the bridge user needs Browse Projects on every bound project.
